the crystal structure of isotactic alternating styrene carbon mono oxide is very similar to that of syndiotactic copolymer but the different symmetry of the monomeric unit leads to different orientations of the phenyl rings.

the isotactic alternating styrene-carbon monoxide copoly mer has an helical conformation with a pitch almost identical to that of the syndiotactic alternating copoly mer, but with a different orientation of the phenylene groups.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chiral Pd(II)-bioxazoline complex is able to control the stereoselectivity in the copolymerization of carbon monoxide with styrene, and to induce an alternating sequence in the copolymeric chain.
the crystal structure of the optically active alternating copolymer between carbon monoxide and styrene has been determined and refined with a Rietveld procedure.

the chiral catalysts used for the copolymerization are able to induce a high degree of stereospecificity in both the stereochemistry and the conformation of the copolymer chains, which in turn determines the packing of the macromolecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the isotactic alternate copolymer between carbon monoxide and styrene is a highly ordered material, with an ordered chain conformation that is different from that observed in the syndiotactic copolymer, and with a different packing of the phenyl rings, which are not coplanar.

, in the absence of a strong steric effect, the chain conformation of alternating copolymers is determined mainly by the symmetry connecting the monomer units and not by the stereochemistry of the polymerization.

the crystal structure of isotactic alternating copolymers is very similar to the crystal structure of syndiotactic copolymer and that the main difference is the relative orientation of the monomers within each chain.
